name: QA Engineer
description: Design tests and catch bugs before users do.

categories.name: Testing Fundamentals
categories.description: Core QA vocabulary, levels of testing, and lifecycle basics.

cards.question: What is the difference between QA and QC?
cards.answer: QA focuses on process improvement to prevent defects; QC focuses on finding defects in the product. QA shapes how work is done; QC validates outputs against requirements. Both contribute to quality but at different layers.

cards.question: What is a test case?
cards.answer: Documented steps, data, and expected result verifying a requirement. Good cases are atomic, repeatable, and traceable to specs. Maintain them as living documents when features evolve.

cards.question: Explain verification vs validation.
cards.answer: Verification asks did we build it right against specs; validation asks did we build the right thing for user needs. Reviews and inspections verify; UAT validates business fit. Both are necessary before release.

cards.question: What is regression testing?
cards.answer: Re-running tests after changes to ensure existing behavior still works. Scope grows with product size— automate the stable core. Risk-based selection prevents endless full regression every sprint.

cards.question: What is exploratory testing?
cards.answer: Simultaneous learning, test design, and execution without heavy scripts. Charters time-box missions on risky areas. Complements scripted tests for unknown unknowns.

cards.question: Define smoke vs sanity testing.
cards.answer: Smoke is a shallow pass on critical paths after a build. Sanity is narrower, focused on a changed area after a fix. Both are quick gates before deeper testing.

cards.question: What is a defect life cycle?
cards.answer: States like New, Assigned, Fixed, Retest, Closed track progress. Rejected or Deferred need documented reasons. Clear workflow prevents lost bugs and duplicate reports.

cards.question: What is equivalence partitioning?
cards.answer: Divide inputs into classes expected to behave similarly and pick one representative per class. Reduces redundant cases while maintaining coverage. Invalid partitions deserve equal attention.

cards.question: What is boundary value analysis?
cards.answer: Defects cluster at edges of valid ranges— test min, max, just inside and outside. Pair with equivalence classes for numeric and date fields. Off-by-one errors are common catches.

cards.question: What is UAT?
cards.answer: End users or product owners validate the system against business scenarios before go-live. UAT sign-off is often contractual. Prepare realistic data and environments mirroring production constraints.

cards.question: Explain test environment parity.
cards.answer: Environments should match prod topology and integrations closely enough to trust results. Over-simplified staging hides integration bugs. Document acceptable differences like scaled-down hardware.

cards.question: What is a test plan?
cards.answer: Scope, approach, resources, schedule, and exit criteria for a test effort. It aligns stakeholders on what will and will not be tested. Update when scope or timelines shift materially.

cards.question: What is ad hoc testing?
cards.answer: Informal testing without documentation— useful for quick feedback but not repeatable. Capture interesting findings into formal cases afterward. Not a substitute for planned coverage on releases.

cards.question: Define severity vs priority of bugs.
cards.answer: Severity is impact on system or users; priority is order of fixing given business context. A cosmetic bug can be high priority near a launch. Document both separately in the tracker.

cards.question: What is RTM?
cards.answer: Requirements Traceability Matrix maps requirements to test cases ensuring coverage. Gaps show untested requirements before release. Maintain links when requirements split or merge.

cards.question: What is alpha vs beta testing?
cards.answer: Alpha is internal pre-release; beta is limited external users in real conditions. Beta feedback drives polish before GA. Monitor crashes and support channels closely during beta.

cards.question: Explain positive vs negative testing.
cards.answer: Positive confirms expected behavior with valid inputs. Negative probes invalid inputs, permissions, and error handling. Security and robustness depend heavily on negative cases.

cards.question: What is test data management?
cards.answer: Realistic, privacy-safe data fuels meaningful tests. Mask or synthesize PII for non-prod. Refresh schedules prevent stale schemas diverging from prod.

cards.question: What is a blocking bug?
cards.answer: Prevents further testing of a major area until fixed. Mark clearly in reports to adjust schedule. Distinguish from critical user-facing defects affecting release go/no-go.

cards.question: What is entry and exit criteria?
cards.answer: Entry defines prerequisites to start testing; exit defines conditions to stop such as pass rate and open sev thresholds. Agreed upfront avoids endless test cycles. Stakeholders sign exit for release decisions.

cards.question: Explain static vs dynamic testing.
cards.answer: Static reviews requirements and code without execution— inspections, walkthroughs. Dynamic runs the software with inputs. Early static catches cheap defects before build costs accumulate.

cards.question: What is compatibility testing?
cards.answer: Verify app behavior across browsers, OS versions, devices, and resolutions per matrix. Prioritize matrix rows by analytics traffic share. Automate top combinations first.

cards.question: What is localization testing?
cards.answer: Validate translations, formats, currencies, and RTL layouts for target locales. Pseudo-localization finds truncation issues early. Legal text may need native speaker review.

cards.question: What is accessibility testing basics?
cards.answer: Check keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, contrast ratios, and ARIA roles against WCAG targets. Automated tools catch ~30 percent; manual review required for flows. Include disabled users in UAT when possible.

cards.question: What is a test oracle?
cards.answer: Mechanism to determine pass or fail— expected output, spec, or another trusted program. Ambiguous oracles cause false passes. Define oracles before executing long suites.

cards.question: What is risk-based testing?
cards.answer: Allocate effort proportional to failure impact and likelihood. High-risk modules get deeper coverage; low-risk get smoke only. Reassess risk each release as architecture changes.

cards.question: Explain white box vs black box.
cards.answer: White box uses internal structure knowledge for path coverage. Black box tests externally without code visibility. Gray box mixes both— typical for API testers with schema knowledge.

cards.question: What is a test harness?
cards.answer: Infrastructure scaffolding executing tests and collecting results— runners, fixtures, and reporting. A good harness isolates flakiness sources. Invest once; all suites benefit.

cards.question: What is confirmation testing?
cards.answer: Retest a fixed defect on the same build or next to verify the fix. Also called re-testing. Distinct from regression which checks surrounding areas.

cards.question: What is a test summary report?
cards.answer: Summarizes execution results, defects, coverage gaps, and recommendation for stakeholders. Written for decision makers not only engineers. Honest about deferred scope builds trust.

categories.name: Test Design
categories.description: Techniques to choose cases, cover risks, and model system behavior.

cards.question: What is decision table testing?
cards.answer: Tables map combinations of conditions to expected actions, ideal for business rules. Reduces missed combinations versus ad hoc cases. Maintain tables when rules change.

cards.question: Explain state transition testing.
cards.answer: Model states and valid transitions; test disallowed transitions too. Good for workflows like order status. Diagrams communicate coverage to non-testers.

cards.question: What is pairwise testing?
cards.answer: Covers all pairs of parameter values with fewer cases than full factorial. Tools generate orthogonal arrays. Apply when interactions between two factors dominate failures.

cards.question: What is use case testing?
cards.answer: Derives scenarios from actor goals in use case documents. Covers main and alternate flows including exceptions. Keeps tests aligned with user journeys.

cards.question: How do you test error messages?
cards.answer: Verify clarity, correct code, no stack traces to users, and safe wording without leaking internals. Localization applies to errors too. Log detailed errors server-side only.

cards.question: What is combinatorial explosion problem?
cards.answer: Full Cartesian product of parameters grows unwieldy. Pairwise or risk-based sampling pragmatically limits count. Document assumed independence when simplifying.

cards.question: Explain CRUD test design.
cards.answer: Create, Read, Update, Delete operations each need happy and sad paths. Permissions differ per operation— test role matrix. Idempotent deletes and duplicate creates deserve cases.

cards.question: What is session and cookie testing?
cards.answer: Expiry, secure and HttpOnly flags, rotation on login, and fixation resistance. Test logout invalidates server session. Cross-subdomain cookie scope causes subtle bugs.

cards.question: How do you design tests for pagination?
cards.answer: First page, last page, empty result, page size boundaries, and concurrent updates during paging. Stable sort keys prevent duplicates across pages. Cursor tokens need expiry cases.

cards.question: What is domain testing?
cards.answer: Focus on input domains from specifications— types, ranges, and constraints. Combines equivalence and boundary techniques formally. Useful for calculation-heavy modules.

cards.question: Explain cause-effect graphing.
cards.answer: Links causes (inputs) to effects (outputs) then converts to decision tables. Finds redundant or missing rule cases. Helps when requirements are rule-heavy.

cards.question: What is checklist-based testing?
cards.answer: Experience-based lists for areas like installation or compatibility. Fast for releases with stable products. Update checklists after incidents reveal gaps.

cards.question: How do you test date and time?
cards.answer: Time zones, DST transitions, leap years, and clock skew scenarios. Never assume server local time equals user zone. Use frozen clocks in unit tests where possible.

cards.question: What is pairwise vs orthogonal array?
cards.answer: Both reduce combination count; orthogonal arrays have mathematical structure for specific strengths. Choose based on parameter count and interaction order assumed. Document coverage strength in test plan.

cards.question: Design tests for file upload.
cards.answer: Size limits, type allow list, virus scan hook, duplicate names, and interrupted uploads. Verify storage path authorization between tenants. Progress and cancel UX need cases too.

cards.question: What is tour testing?
cards.answer: Guided exploratory tours like money tour or config tour across the app. Each tour focuses on a theme. Time-box and debrief findings into tickets.

cards.question: How do you test role-based access?
cards.answer: Matrix of roles vs actions with positive and negative cells. Horizontal escalation between users same role level. Default-deny for new features until roles updated.

cards.question: What is error guessing?
cards.answer: Experience predicts where developers often fail— nulls, division by zero, empty strings. Not systematic alone but seeds exploratory charters. Pair juniors with seniors for knowledge transfer.

cards.question: Explain model-based testing.
cards.answer: Abstract model generates tests automatically for transitions or data flows. Upfront modeling cost pays off on stable complex domains. Tools vary in learning curve.

cards.question: How do you test search functionality?
cards.answer: Exact match, partial, fuzzy, special characters, SQL injection strings safely, empty query, and performance on large indexes. Highlighting and sort order need expectations.

cards.question: What is thread safety testing?
cards.answer: Concurrent operations on shared resources under load or scripted parallelism. Race bugs are intermittent— stress repeats help. Use tools appropriate to stack.

cards.question: Design cases for payment flows.
cards.answer: Success, decline, timeout, idempotent retry, partial capture, refund, and webhook ordering. Never use real cards in test— use provider sandboxes. PCI scope stays out of dev laptops.

cards.question: What is heuristic test strategy?
cards.answer: Heuristics like SFDPOT or RCRCRC guide exploratory coverage dimensions. They are mnemonics not replacements for requirements trace. Share heuristics in team wiki.

cards.question: How do you test caching?
cards.answer: Verify cache hit/miss behavior, TTL expiry, invalidation on update, and stale reads acceptable by design. CDN cache headers differ from app cache. Purge APIs need authorization tests.

cards.question: What is A/B test validation?
cards.answer: Ensure assignment consistency, metric collection, and no cross-contamination between variants. QA confirms experiment toggles off restores control behavior. Statistical analysis is product; QA guards implementation integrity.

cards.question: Explain boundary on string fields.
cards.answer: Min length, max length, unicode, emoji, trimming, and null vs empty string semantics. Database column limits may truncate silently. Validation messages should match spec.

cards.question: How do you test email notifications?
cards.answer: Trigger conditions, template content, links, unsubscribe compliance, and delivery in sandbox inboxes. Async delays require polling or webhooks in tests. Localization of templates included.

cards.question: What is soap opera testing?
cards.answer: Long realistic scenarios chaining many steps mimicking dramatic user days. Finds integration and state accumulation bugs. Expensive— run on major releases or nightly.

cards.question: Design tests for offline mode.
cards.answer: Queue actions offline, sync on reconnect, conflict resolution rules, and user messaging. Airplane mode on mobile devices for manual passes. Automate API stubs simulating disconnect.

cards.question: What is charter for exploratory session?
cards.answer: Mission, scope, time box, and notes template for one session. Review charters in group debriefs. Metrics: areas covered and issues filed.

categories.name: Test Automation
categories.description: Frameworks, stability, CI integration, and maintainable automated checks.

cards.question: What should you automate first?
cards.answer: Stable high-value smoke and core regressions with clear oracles. Avoid automating volatile UI experiments early. ROI rises when tests run every commit.

cards.question: Explain the test automation pyramid.
cards.answer: Many unit tests, fewer integration, thin UI E2E on top. Inverted pyramids slow CI and flake. Adjust per architecture but keep fast feedback base wide.

cards.question: What is page object model?
cards.answer: Encapsulate locators and actions per page or component. UI changes update one class not every test. Keep objects small and composable.

cards.question: How do you reduce flaky UI tests?
cards.answer: Stable data-testid selectors, explicit waits on conditions, isolated data per test. Quarantine flakes until root-caused. Retries mask problems— fix causality.

cards.question: When prefer API tests over UI?
cards.answer: API tests validate business rules faster with less brittleness. UI covers layout and cross-browser journeys. Combine API setup with thin UI smoke.

cards.question: What is CI integration for automation?
cards.answer: Run smoke on PR; fuller suite on main or nightly. Parallel shards with junit merge. Collect screenshots and logs on failure artifacts.

cards.question: Explain test data factories.
cards.answer: Programmatic builders create entities with sensible defaults and overrides. Faster than static JSON fixtures drifting from schema. Tear down or use unique IDs in shared envs.

cards.question: What is BDD with Gherkin?
cards.answer: Given-When-Then scenarios readable by stakeholders executed by Cucumber or similar. Keep steps reusable not one-off prose per case. Living documentation when synced with code.

cards.question: How do you handle async in tests?
cards.answer: Await proper conditions not fixed sleeps. Poll with timeout and clear failure messages. Framework-specific async utilities beat busy loops.

cards.question: What is visual regression testing?
cards.answer: Screenshot compare detects unintended UI shifts. Baseline updates need review not blind approve. Mask dynamic regions like timestamps.

cards.question: Explain parallel test isolation.
cards.answer: Each worker owns data namespace or database schema. Shared mutable state causes order-dependent failures. Containerized dependencies per job help.

cards.question: What is contract test in automation context?
cards.answer: Consumer-driven contracts verify provider compatibility without full E2E. Run in CI for both sides. Complements but does not replace critical path E2E.

cards.question: How do you version test code?
cards.answer: Same repo or mono-repo adjacent to app with PR review. Tag releases with app versions for traceability. Deprecate obsolete tests actively.

cards.question: What is keyword-driven framework?
cards.answer: Tests compose reusable keywords mapping to actions. Non-coders can assemble scenarios in spreadsheets— tradeoff maintenance cost. Modern code-first frameworks often replace this.

cards.question: Explain mocking external services.
cards.answer: Stub third parties unavailable in CI with WireMock or similar. Over-mocking hides integration bugs— reserve for true externals. Record-replay helps realistic stubs.

cards.question: What is mobile automation difference?
cards.answer: Appium drives native and hybrid apps with platform-specific capabilities. Device farms or emulators in CI. Flakier than web— invest in stable locators.

cards.question: How do you test microservices in automation?
cards.answer: Service-level contract and integration tests per boundary plus selective E2E through gateway. Testcontainers spin real databases in JVM tests. Map failures to owning team quickly.

cards.question: What is shift-left in automation?
cards.answer: Developers write unit and component tests; QA focuses integration and risk charters. Pair on missing unit coverage for complex modules. Fail builds on agreed coverage drops in critical paths.

cards.question: Explain reporting for automation failures.
cards.answer: Clear step, URL, screenshot, network log, and build ID in report. Link to known flake tickets. Separate infra failures from product defects in dashboards.

cards.question: What is self-healing locators?
cards.answer: ML adjusts broken selectors— use cautiously. Can hide real UI regressions if abused. Prefer stable design-for-test attributes from devs.

cards.question: How do you maintain automation debt?
cards.answer: Regular prune of obsolete tests and refactor duplicated helpers. Track maintenance time vs value in retros. Delete tests that never fail but cost run time.

cards.question: What is Playwright vs Selenium?
cards.answer: Playwright offers auto-wait, tracing, and modern browser automation APIs. Selenium has broader legacy grid ecosystems. Pick based on team skills and browser matrix.

cards.question: Explain test tagging.
cards.answer: Tags like @smoke @regression filter CI jobs. Document tag meanings in README. Avoid tag explosion without ownership.

cards.question: What is headless CI execution?
cards.answer: Browsers run without UI faster in pipelines. Some bugs appear only headed— schedule periodic headed runs. GPU and font differences rarely affect functional tests.

cards.question: How do you automate accessibility checks?
cards.answer: axe-core integration in E2E catches many violations. Manual keyboard passes still required for compliance sign-off. Fail CI on critical a11y violations when policy matures.

cards.question: What is data-driven testing?
cards.answer: Same test logic iterates rows from CSV or JSON datasets. Separates data from code for clarity. Validate schema of data files in CI too.

cards.question: Explain hybrid automation.
cards.answer: Mix vendor codeless tools with custom code for complex flows. Governance prevents siloed unmaintainable scripts. Central patterns library helps.

cards.question: What is flake detection analytics?
cards.answer: Track tests that fail then pass without code change. Rank by flake rate for fixing priority. Some CI products compute automatically.

cards.question: How do you test feature flags in automation?
cards.answer: Parameterize runs with flag on/off matrices for affected suites. Clean up flag-specific tests when flag removed. Mock flag service in unit layer.

cards.question: What is automation exit criteria?
cards.answer: Agreed coverage of regression catalog, stable pass rate over N runs, and run time within CI budget. Document manual-only areas explicitly. Revisit each major architecture change.

categories.name: API Testing
categories.description: REST and API verification, contracts, auth, and integration checks.

cards.question: What do REST API tests verify beyond status codes?
cards.answer: Schema, headers, body fields, pagination, and error contract for invalid inputs. Idempotency and rate limits where specified. Compare responses to OpenAPI spec automatically.

cards.question: How test authentication on APIs?
cards.answer: Missing token, expired token, wrong scope, and horizontal access between users. Error bodies must not leak stack traces. Automate role matrices as data-driven tests.

cards.question: What is Postman/Newman in CI?
cards.answer: Collections executable headless in pipelines with environment files. Newman reports junit for gates. Keep secrets in CI variables not committed collections.

cards.question: Explain JSON schema validation.
cards.answer: Assert response matches schema for types and required fields. Catches silent field drops in releases. Version schemas with API semver.

cards.question: How do you test GraphQL APIs?
cards.answer: Validate correct data shape, error extensions, query cost limits, and authorization per field. Introspection disabled in prod should be tested in staging policy. Batch queries for load characteristics.

cards.question: What is idempotency key testing?
cards.answer: Repeat POST with same key should not duplicate side effects. Verify server returns same result on replay. Critical for payment and order APIs.

cards.question: How test file upload APIs?
cards.answer: Size cap, MIME validation, checksum, virus scan stub, and unauthorized download attempts. Multipart boundary edge cases. Resume interrupted upload if supported.

cards.question: What is OAuth2 flow testing?
cards.answer: Authorization code, client credentials, refresh rotation, and revoked token behavior. PKCE required for public clients. Never log tokens in test output.

cards.question: Explain contract testing with Pact.
cards.answer: Consumer defines expected interactions; provider verifies in CI. Catches breaking changes early. Provider states setup test data carefully.

cards.question: How do you test webhooks?
cards.answer: Expose test receiver; assert payload signature, retry backoff, and ordering. Simulate provider downtime and duplicate deliveries. Idempotent processing required on consumer side.

cards.question: What is negative API testing?
cards.answer: Malformed JSON, wrong content-type, overflow fields, and injection strings safely in test env. Expect consistent error format and HTTP codes per spec. Document undocumented 500s as bugs.

cards.question: How test API versioning?
cards.answer: Old clients on v1 still work while v2 ships; sunset headers communicated. Breaking changes only in major version. Integration tests pin both versions during transition.

cards.question: What is load testing APIs separately?
cards.answer: Functional pass first; then k6 or Gatling on representative endpoints. Watch error rate under load not just latency. Shared staging hardware skews results— note environment.

cards.question: Explain HATEOAS testing if used.
cards.answer: Links in responses navigate workflow states correctly. Broken hrefs block clients relying on discovery. Less common in modern JSON APIs but test if promised.

cards.question: How do you test rate limiting?
cards.answer: Exceed quota and expect 429 with Retry-After header. Different limits per API key tier. Reset window behavior documented and verified.

cards.question: What is chakram/supertest style?
cards.answer: In-process HTTP tests against app without network hop for speed. Good for Node Express layers. Still need separate contract tests against deployed env.

cards.question: How test pagination cursors?
cards.answer: Walk until empty; no duplicates on static dataset. Invalid cursor returns safe error. Concurrent writes document expected anomalies.

cards.question: What is SOAP API testing basics?
cards.answer: WSDL defines operations; XML assert nodes and faults. Still prevalent in enterprise integrations. Tools like SoapUI generate baseline requests.

cards.question: Explain mTLS client cert tests.
cards.answer: Present valid, expired, and wrong CN certs expecting pass or fail appropriately. Revocation checking if enabled. Automate cert generation in fixture scripts.

cards.question: How do you mock time-dependent APIs?
cards.answer: Freeze clock injection or test hooks returning fixed timestamps. Token expiry boundaries need controlled time. Avoid flaky midnight failures.

cards.question: What is API fuzz testing?
cards.answer: Randomized inputs hunt crashes and 500 errors. Run in isolated env with monitoring. Findings triaged separately from functional suite.

cards.question: How test bulk endpoints?
cards.answer: Partial success responses, batch size limits, and transactional semantics all-or-nothing vs best-effort. Timeout on huge payloads. Document max items per request.

cards.question: What is header contract testing?
cards.answer: ETag, Cache-Control, Correlation-Id, and Content-Type must match spec. Missing security headers flagged in security suite. CORS preflight OPTIONS covered.

cards.question: Explain testing gRPC services.
cards.answer: Protobuf contracts version carefully; breaking field changes fail compatibility checks. grpcurl for manual; automated clients in same language often faster. Status codes map from rich error model.

cards.question: How do you test long polling or SSE?
cards.answer: Hold connection open; assert events sequence and reconnect behavior. Timeouts and proxy buffering issues appear in staging. Automate with client libraries supporting async read.

cards.question: What is consumer-driven contract ownership?
cards.answer: Consumer team publishes pacts; provider CI verifies. Communication channel for evolving fields. Prevents integration surprise on deploy day.

cards.question: How test API localization?
cards.answer: Accept-Language header switches message strings and formatted dates. Fallback locale when unsupported. Error messages localized consistently with UI.

cards.question: What is snapshot testing for JSON?
cards.answer: Compare full response to stored golden file— brittle if data volatile. Use selective field assertions instead for dynamic IDs. Snapshots ok for stable reference payloads.

cards.question: Explain testing DELETE safety.
cards.answer: Soft delete vs hard delete semantics. Unauthorized delete returns 403 not 404 information leak. Cascade rules on related resources verified.

cards.question: How do you organize API test folders?
cards.answer: By resource or user journey mirroring product domains. Shared auth fixture at suite level. Clear naming maps failures to owning squad.

categories.name: Performance & Security Testing
categories.description: Load and resilience testing plus security validation within QA scope.

cards.question: What is performance testing goal?
cards.answer: Validate response time, throughput, and stability under expected and peak load. Find bottlenecks before users do. Define success criteria before running tools.

cards.question: Explain load vs stress vs soak.
cards.answer: Load is expected traffic; stress exceeds limits to find breaking point; soak holds moderate load for hours exposing leaks. Each answers different risk questions. Schedule soak before major releases.

cards.question: What metrics matter in perf tests?
cards.answer: p95/p99 latency, error rate, throughput, and resource utilization on app and DB. Averages hide tail pain. Compare against SLO targets not arbitrary numbers.

cards.question: How do you design perf scenarios?
cards.answer: Model think time and mix from production analytics. Ramp up gradually to observe scaling curve. Seed realistic data volume not empty databases.

cards.question: What causes misleading perf results?
cards.answer: Cold cache, tiny datasets, shared staging hardware, and disabled features unlike prod. Warm up before measuring. Document environmental assumptions in report.

cards.question: Explain baseline and benchmark.
cards.answer: Baseline captures current release; future runs compare regressions. Store results in trend database. Alert on threshold regression in CI for critical endpoints.

cards.question: What is security testing in QA scope?
cards.answer: Validate authZ, input validation, session handling, and security headers within test charters. Not full pentest replacement but catches obvious gaps. Escalate findings with severity like functional bugs.

cards.question: What is OWASP Top 10 relevance?
cards.answer: Common web risks like injection and broken access control guide test ideas. Map cases to categories in test plan. Developers fix; QA verifies mitigations.

cards.question: How test SQL injection safely?
cards.answer: Use known safe payloads in test env only producing expected errors or sanitization. Never on production. Automated DAST tools supplement manual vectors.

cards.question: What is XSS testing approach?
cards.answer: Inject script strings in reflected and stored contexts expecting encoding or CSP block. Verify DOM-based XSS in rich client apps. Report bypasses with reproduction steps minimally exposing users.

cards.question: Explain CSRF protection testing.
cards.answer: State-changing requests without token should fail. SameSite cookies and double-submit patterns verified. Login CSRF also considered on sensitive apps.

cards.question: What is penetration test handoff?
cards.answer: QA shares test accounts, scope URLs, and known integrations before external pentest. Retest fixes before closure report. Duplicate pentest findings become regression cases where feasible.

cards.question: How do you test session timeout?
cards.answer: Idle and absolute timeout expirations redirect to login. Sensitive actions re-auth if required. Concurrent session policy per product spec.

cards.question: What is security regression suite?
cards.answer: Automated checks for auth matrix, headers, and known CVE patches after upgrades. Run smaller suite on each release. Complement annual pentest.

cards.question: Explain performance NFR traceability.
cards.answer: Non-functional requirements link to perf test cases like max concurrent users. Sign off when NFRs met or waivers approved. Product owns NFR definitions.

cards.question: What tools for load testing?
cards.answer: k6, JMeter, Gatling chosen by team skills and protocol support. Distributed generators for large scale. Monitor server side during runs not only client stats.

cards.question: How test TLS and cipher config?
cards.answer: testssl or SSL Labs on staging public endpoints. Weak protocols should fail policy. Cert expiry monitored same as functional monitors.

cards.question: What is race condition security bug?
cards.answer: Double spend or duplicate grant under parallel requests. Automate parallel curl or scripted threads in test env. Fix often needs transactional locking on server.

cards.question: Explain data exposure in API errors.
cards.answer: Errors must not reveal stack, SQL, or internal IDs unnecessarily. QA cases probe verbose error modes disabled in prod config. Log server-side detail instead.

cards.question: What is performance test environment?
cards.answer: Dedicated hardware or isolated cloud stack sized like prod fraction. Contention from other teams invalidates numbers. Label reports with env fingerprint.

cards.question: How test brute force protections?
cards.answer: Account lockout or CAPTCHA after N failures. Rate limit by IP and account. Verify lockout reset and support unlock flow.

cards.question: What is sensitive data in logs QA check?
cards.answer: Search logs during tests for credit cards or passwords accidentally logged. Automated grep patterns in log review checklist. Fail release if PII found in debug enabled prod.

cards.question: Explain scalability testing.
cards.answer: Increase load until linear scaling breaks identifying first bottleneck. Often database connections or thread pools. Results feed capacity planning.

cards.question: What is client-side perf testing?
cards.answer: Lighthouse metrics for web— LCP, CLS, INP. Mobile app startup time and memory. Set budgets in CI for critical pages where tooling supports.

cards.question: How do you test CDN behavior?
cards.answer: Cache hit ratio, purge effectiveness, and geo routing. Stale content after deploy mitigated by purge automation. Origin shield under load tested.

cards.question: What is security chaos idea?
cards.answer: Game days injecting revoked certs or expired tokens in staging. Validates monitoring and graceful degradation. Coordinate with SRE to avoid false prod alerts.

cards.question: Explain perf test data volume.
cards.answer: Tests on empty DB mislead query planner behavior. Seed proportional rows to prod tables. Anonymized prod subset import common approach.

cards.question: What is vulnerability scanning in QA pipeline?
cards.answer: Dependency and container scans gate releases on critical CVEs. WAivers need expiry and owner. QA tracks scan dashboard like test dashboards.

cards.question: How test content security policy?
cards.answer: Verify inline scripts blocked when CSP enforced. Report-only mode first in staging. Breakages caught before enforce breaks prod UI.

cards.question: What is perf sign-off criteria?
cards.answer: All NFR scenarios pass thresholds, no critical resource leaks in soak, and no regression beyond agreed percent from baseline. Document residual risks if waivers exist.

categories.name: Process & Soft Skills
categories.description: Defect lifecycle, collaboration, metrics, and release communication.

cards.question: What makes a good bug report?
cards.answer: Clear title, minimal repro steps, expected vs actual, environment, logs, and severity. Attach screenshots or HAR when useful. Link requirement or build for bisect.

cards.question: How do severity and priority differ?
cards.answer: Severity is user or system impact; priority is fix order given business context. Document both fields separately. Revisit priority as release date nears.

cards.question: What metrics help QA without gaming?
cards.answer: Escaped defects, cycle time to fix, flaky rate trends, and coverage of risk areas. Avoid raw case count vanity metrics. Pair numbers with qualitative release notes.

cards.question: Explain definition of done for QA.
cards.answer: Acceptance criteria met, agreed automation updated, docs refreshed, no open blockers for scope. QA signs on evidence not activity. Embedded in workflow tool checklist.

cards.question: What is shift-left testing?
cards.answer: Involve QA in requirements and design reviews early. Write test ideas before code merges. Cheaper defects found upstream.

cards.question: How handle is-it-a-bug disagreements?
cards.answer: Refer to specs and product owner for ambiguous behavior. Document decision for consistency. Reproduction video reduces debate.

cards.question: What belongs in test summary for executives?
cards.answer: Scope, pass/fail by area, open defects by severity, go/no-go recommendation, and deferred risks. Plain language outcomes. No jargon without explanation.

cards.question: How manage regression across frequent releases?
cards.answer: Risk-based catalog tagged by feature and failure history. Automate core; rotate exploratory on changes. Retire obsolete cases.

cards.question: What is root cause analysis after escape?
cards.answer: Timeline introduction to detection gap; corrective actions on tests and process. Blameless tone encourages honesty. Track action item completion.

cards.question: How coordinate QA with continuous delivery?
cards.answer: Fast automated gates, feature flags, and monitoring as safety net. QA charters risks per change rather than big-bang signoff. Evidence-based release decisions.

cards.question: Explain three amigos meeting.
cards.answer: Dev, QA, and product refine story acceptance together before sprint work. Shared understanding reduces rework. Minutes capture edge cases discovered.

cards.question: What is test strategy document?
cards.answer: High-level approach for program or release— scope, tools, environments, and risks. Differs from detailed test plan per phase. Living doc updated annually or on architecture shifts.

cards.question: How do you estimate testing effort?
cards.answer: Break by feature risk, automation reuse, and env setup needs. Historical velocity on similar stories helps. Buffer for integration unknowns explicitly.

cards.question: What is quality gate?
cards.answer: Objective criteria blocking promotion— pass rate, open sev1 count, perf thresholds. Automated where possible. Waivers require named approver.

cards.question: Explain bug triage meeting.
cards.answer: Regular review of new defects prioritizing and assigning. Duplicate detection and severity calibration happen here. Time-box to keep flow moving.

cards.question: What is whole team quality?
cards.answer: Testing is everyone's job; QA coaches and focuses on risk. Developers own unit tests; ops owns prod monitoring feedback loop. Reduces QA bottleneck myth.

cards.question: How communicate release risk?
cards.answer: Residual risk list with mitigations and monitoring plans. Honest no-go saves reputation. Post-release hypercare when risk accepted.

cards.question: What is pairing dev and QA?
cards.answer: QA pairs on story implementation clarifying acceptance live. Shortens feedback loop within sprint. Builds mutual respect and shared ownership.

cards.question: Explain test debt.
cards.answer: Skipped automation, outdated cases, and missing env parity accumulate interest. Schedule paydown sprints like tech debt. Track visibly in backlog.

cards.question: What is crowdtesting?
cards.answer: External testers on real devices and locales supplement core team. Good for diversity of exploration. Manage NDAs and data privacy carefully.

cards.question: How onboard new QA to product?
cards.answer: Structured domain doc, shadowing incidents, and guided bug fixes first weeks. Buddy assigns increasing charter complexity. Feedback loop on documentation gaps.

cards.question: What is compliance testing?
cards.answer: Validate regulatory requirements— audit trails, retention, consent flows. Checklists from legal mapped to cases. Evidence pack for auditors on request.

cards.question: Explain stakeholder management for QA.
cards.answer: Regular status without alarmism; escalate blockers early. Translate technical risk to business impact language. Build trust with consistent quality signals.

cards.question: What is hypercare post-release?
cards.answer: Increased monitoring and rapid response window after major launch. QA on standby for quick verification of hotfixes. Defined duration and exit to normal support.

cards.question: How do you say no to unsafe release?
cards.answer: Present data— open defects, untested areas, perf regressions. Offer options— scope cut, flag off, delay. Document decision makers accepting risk if override.

cards.question: What is learning from production bugs?
cards.answer: Each escape gets retrospective test or monitor addition. Trend analysis on component hotspots. Close loop visible to team morale.

cards.question: Explain QA in Agile ceremonies.
cards.answer: Active in planning, refinement, standup blockers, review demos, retro process tweaks. Skip-only when truly no test impact that sprint. Voice risk early in planning poker.

cards.question: What is cross-functional release checklist?
cards.answer: Dev, QA, ops, support sign items— migrations run, comms sent, rollback tested. Single shared doc per release train. Prevents forgotten toggle or doc update.

cards.question: How maintain domain knowledge as QA?
cards.answer: Notes on integrations, quirks, and historical incidents in team wiki. Rotate feature ownership among QA members. Avoid single bus factor on complex modules.

cards.question: What is ethical responsibility of QA?
cards.answer: Report quality issues honestly even under schedule pressure. Protect user privacy in test data handling. Speak up when safety or compliance at stake.
